question: Is it wrong to have sex outside of marriage?
summary: The Torah (Exod 20:14, Deut 5:18) and the New Testament (Acts 15:20, 1 Cor 5:1, 6:13, 6:18, 10:8, 2 Cor 12:21, Gal 5:19-21, Eph 5:3, Col 3:5-6, 1 Thess 4:3, Heb 13:4, Jude 7) repeatedly condemn fornication and adultery. But Hosea 1:2 and 3:1 have YHWH commanding the prophet Hosea to take a "wife of whoredoms" and later to love an adulteress — God explicitly commanding the act his own law forbids.

reconcile.connective: Defenders read God's order to Hosea not as a license to fornicate but either as a vision/enacted parable that never literally occurred, or as a marriage made lawful by the divine command itself.

discrepancy.connective: The objection is pressed by Steve Wells, who catalogues Hosea 1:2 as God ordering the prophet to take a "wife of whoredoms," i.e., commanding the very adultery his own law forbids.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.attribution: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible (2013); skepticsannotatedbible.com

pd_work.resource: Keil & Delitzsch, Biblical Commentary on the Old Testament (1861-75), on Hosea 1:2 and 3:1
pd_work.author: Keil & Delitzsch
pd_work.note: K&D treat this passage directly, arguing the command was of a 'purely symbolical character' that 'did not contemplate an actual and outward marriage,' and so does not enjoin the conduct the law forbids.

link.title: GotQuestions: Why did God tell Hosea to marry a prostitute (Hosea 1:2)?
link.note: Live apologetic treatment reading the marriage command as a divinely-purposed symbolic illustration of Israel's unfaithfulness rather than sanctioned immorality.

excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly answers the conflict: the command was not an actual act of taking a harlot but a vision/parable, so no real fornication was commanded.
excerpts.source_note_text: That is, one that of long time hath accustomed to play the harlot: not that the Prophet did this thing in effect, but he saw this in a vision, or else was commanded by God to set forth under this parable or figure the idolatry of the Synagogue, and of the people her children.
